name: Projection Depth Taxonomy Registry
purpose: Classify projection operators by structural flattening depth and retained fidelity to simultaneous recursive aspect-binding.

depth_levels.name: shallow_projection
depth_levels.definition: Projection retains source traceability, aspect context, and limited residue metadata while reducing expression complexity.

depth_levels.name: moderate_projection
depth_levels.definition: Projection retains source traceability but abstracts simultaneity into directional, comparative, or local symbolic form.

depth_levels.name: deep_projection
depth_levels.definition: Projection produces ordinary symbolic structures such as equality, implication, composition, or biconditional while preserving only minimal source traceability.
depth_levels.reconstruction_warning: Source reconstruction is not available from projected form alone.

depth_levels.name: terminal_projection
depth_levels.definition: Projection output is highly flattened and cannot be used to reconstruct the source relation except through external trace metadata.

operator_depth_assignments.reason: Equality flattens recursive binding into restricted substitutability.
Composition orders indivisible co-presence into structural chaining.
Logical biconditional retains reciprocal truth readability but loses residue-bound closure.

depth_governance_rules.rule: PD-3 and PD-4 projections require explicit warning that source reconstruction is not available from projected form alone.
PD-4 projections may not be used as evidence for primitive relation structure.
Higher depth implies higher flattening risk and stricter loss accounting.

forbidden_uses: Using deep projections as primitive evidence.
Using projection depth to promote physical or theorem claims.
